executiveSummary.line: New CTO Steve Habermas — AI, ERP, robotics, factory data
June billings — first $8M month of the year
Headcount climbing; glue line still hiring

sections.title: Leadership & Organizational Updates
bullets: Steve Habermas — new CTO leading AI, ERP integration, factory data collection, and robotics. Onsite Hauppauge this week; Roanoke full-time starting following Monday.
Travelex replaces prior travel agency (Grace/Graziella after price doubling). 24-hour concierge, online booking, dedicated rep. Starts July 31; rollout August 1.
Marshall McLennan negotiated environmental compliance for Platinum ECHO 2027: ~$250,000 down to $79,000.
Staffing changes: West leaving in 30 days (die cutting); Izzy (top pressman) departing ~8–10 weeks reserve training then returning; Wes departing July 14.

sections.title: Financial Performance
bullets: Estée Lauder bounced back strongly in June after slow May.
L'Oréal down $800,000 YTD; Blue Mercury down $500,000 YTD (first six months).
Mix positive; overtime, freight, and repairs & maintenance headwinds on margin.
Two large assets fully depreciated end of June — ~$80,000/month reversal through year-end.
SG&A unfavorable $69,000 for month: $25,000 LOC renewal fee ($10M facility), higher travel, final R&D tax-refund payment (program yielded $2M savings over recent years).
July pace: $7.4M MTD bookings with ~10 days left; last July finished $6.9M.

sections.title: Factory & SG&A Costs
bullets: Freight expected to double in H2 on fuel/geopolitical pressure.
Consultants include ~$40,000 AI-related; Ricardo $30,000; tax consultants +$18,000.
One additional sales headcount +$40,000 YTD.

sections.title: Production, Capacity & Staffing
bullets: Fully staffed facility could produce ~450M units/year (~$130M sales); ~$100M realistic with current equipment.
Glue line printed ~500,000 sheets in two days; two coding machines now running.
Obsolete inventory: $40,000 approvals through; ~$300,000 from 2025 remains outstanding.
6–8 interviews scheduled; new pressman begins Monday.
Additional equipment investment planned 2027–2028.

sections.title: Quality & Rejects
bullets: June complaints: Innovation Labs, Olaplex, Clinique, Bobby Brown, Native (13,000-carton reject — misplaced die/security tag), P&G (2).
Do-over YTD: 4 jobs, 41,605 units, $22,943 cost (added P&G blister-card SBS vs blister-board mix-up).
Over 50% of new graphic jobs required rework due to imaging/pre-press file errors — urgent daily tracking required.
Olaplex: 127 miscolored/missing-logo cartons in one case; resolved without full rerun. Account ~$1.5M + $600K holiday order at risk.
Leadership: stop production immediately when issues found — no penalty for reporting.

sections.title: Customer & Contract Updates
bullets: Estée Lauder: 18.5% of business vs 22.2% LY (Bobby Brown weakness); price increase pursued; ~$300K aged 2025 liability uncollected.
Oral-B: ramping mid-August; contract extension requested (no cartons since January award).
Crest: single-pass hologram/rainbow effect in progress; beveled carton proof for 2–3 year contract; first sheets Roanoke ~July 27.
Sol de Janeiro: expanding volume (promo + line); new Epson printer; men's fragrance pulling production from China.
P&G: Olay cartons and femcare negotiations; P&G pushing 1-year vs 2–3 year terms.
KDC/One qualifying for US and European work (Unilever, J&J); NDA discussions with Creatures (fragrance collectibles).

sections.title: HR & Benefits
bullets: Captive insurance model (~1.2M lives) vs proposed 13% increase from prior carrier.
Medical: Aetna; dental: Delta Dental; vision: Delta Vision. Enrollment starts August 1.
Production bonuses begin September payout (for August) from existing $400K annual pool (~$170–180K/month allocation).
Hiring event next Thursday (1:30–4:30) targeting displaced workers — process technicians and packers.

actions.action: Send full Travelex travel agency details including dedicated contact by Monday.
Resolve past-due Nest billing; track booking/billing bottlenecks; coordinate production bonus communication.
Lead daily documentation/tracking of file and quality issues; report at next Management Meeting.
Pursue Bobby Brown price increase with Estée Lauder; support onboarding of planner Christian.
Support Global Vision rollout; identify automation for Estée Lauder billing/inventory.
Maintain Olaplex relationship and monitor upcoming orders after quality issues.
Prepare cause-and-effect quality reports; lead inspection efforts to reduce rejects.
Improve Imaging/Prepress QC to reduce high file revision rate.
Aggressive hiring including Voyant event — operators, process technicians, glue line.
Increase glue line staffing 81→95; continue operator training to reduce overtime.
Report production/quality issues immediately — reinforce See Something, Say Something.
